rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent courtyard slab with a clear dominant mass, a single continuous rule, and an obvious public void that relates well to the marked access edge. In all four views the form remains consistent; there is no obvious interpenetration or view-dependent collision, and the parcel is respected without merely filling a box. The strongest quality is the ground-level carve/opening, which gives the neighborhood-living brief an active threshold and a usable open-space figure. The main weakness is the section: it is essentially a low horizontal ring/plate with limited evidence of a richer roof or daylight hierarchy, so it supports the program only moderately well rather than exceptionally. The stepped or sloped silhouette is present but not especially meaningful; it is coherent, yet not a strong sectional program expression. Overall this is a hard pass for program fit because the visible mass can plausibly support a compact neighborhood mixed-use building with public void and active edge.
